q: Is there a closed-form characterisation of the accuracy loss |P(k_opt) - P(k*)| as a function of the fractional part of (pi/4)*sqrt(N), where k_opt is the rounded convention and k* is the per-N optimal integer? Our sweep showed N=4 overshoots (P=0.25 at rounded k=2 vs P=1.0 at k=1) and N=256 loses ~0.014 by rounding k=12 up to k=13.
basis: Statevector sweep over k in [0..k_opt+2] for N in {4,16,64,256} exposed a non-monotonic accuracy pattern induced purely by integer rounding of the standard k_opt = round((pi/4)*sqrt(N)) formula the survey summarises.

q: At what N does the finite-size correction to the O(sqrt(N)) query complexity fall below (say) 1 % of the asymptotic slope? Our log-log fit slope was 0.4551 including N=4 and ~0.500 when N=4 was dropped, suggesting the survey's asymptotic statement precedes a rounding-dominated regime whose extent is not quantified.
basis: Linear fit of log(k_opt) vs log(N) over N in {4,16,64,256} vs the same fit over {16,64,256} shows a clean threshold-like transition to the asymptotic O(sqrt(N)) claimed in Theorem 2.1.

q: The survey treats Grover as noiseless. At what per-gate error rate (under depolarising or amplitude-damping noise) does the theoretical Grover peak at k_opt become statistically indistinguishable from the k=0 baseline probability 1/N, for N in {16, 64, 256}? A noise-threshold sweep would ground the practical relevance of the O(sqrt(N)) claim on near-term devices.
basis: Our statevector reproduction agreed to ~5e-15 with the sin^2((2k+1)theta) formula, i.e. we exercised only the noiseless regime; the survey does not discuss any noise sensitivity of the headline claim.

q: How does the compiled 2-qubit-gate depth of the standard multi-controlled-Z-based Grover oracle+diffuser scale with n, and at what n does that compiled depth dominate the k = O(sqrt(N)) query count in practice? The survey's O(sqrt(N)) counts abstract-oracle queries, hiding the actual per-query gate cost.
basis: Building the oracle via X-sandwiched mcx forced Aer to decompose it into elementary gates; the transpiled circuit depth per iteration is O(n) or worse, which is invisible in the survey's black-box query-complexity framing but matters for real hardware.

q: For M > 1 known marked items, over which (N, M) pairs does the rounded k_opt = round((pi/4)*sqrt(N/M)) still land within (say) 1 % of the true peak of sin^2((2k+1)theta)? Larger M shortens the sin^2 period, sharpening rounding-induced overshoots.
basis: We fixed M=1 for tractability; the survey (Sec. 2.2, Ref. [14]) asserts an M>1 tuned version reaches certainty in O(sqrt(N/M)) but does not chart the rounding-safe regime, which our M=1 sweep already hinted is non-trivial (e.g. N=4).

q: How does measured Grover success probability degrade under realistic depolarising noise as a function of qubit count, and at what noise level does the k = round((pi/4)*sqrt(N)) optimum stop being the empirical optimum?
basis: Our noiseless N=16, N=64 sweeps showed P(k*) matching analytic to within shot noise, so the shape of the P(k) curve is entirely intact; but the paper's Table 3 cites lab-scale N=8 NMR demos, and Montanaro does not indicate at what error-per-gate the k*-picking heuristic starts to select the wrong k (over-rotation dominates once P(k*)-P(k*+/-1) shrinks below the noise-driven flattening).

q: Does the O(sqrt(N)) query-count savings survive when the oracle circuit itself has depth polylog(N) rather than the O(1) idealisation used in complexity accounting?
basis: Our phase oracle is a single multi-controlled-Z per iteration, treated as O(1) in the survey's asymptotic claim; in practice an MCX on n qubits decomposes into O(n) or O(n^2) two-qubit gates depending on ancilla policy, so 'query' complexity and true 2-qubit-gate complexity can diverge and the crossover N with classical SAT solvers is not obvious from the survey alone.

q: For multi-solution unstructured search (M > 1 marked items), how does the observed optimal iteration count k*(N, M) = round((pi/4)*sqrt(N/M)) hold up when M is unknown a priori, i.e. under BBHT amplitude-estimation heuristics?
basis: Montanaro cites 'the extension to multiple solutions came slightly later [18]' in a footnote but does not test it; our replication used a unique-target oracle, and sweeping M in {1,2,4,8} at N=64 would test whether observed argmax tracks (pi/4)*sqrt(N/M) and how shot-noise variance scales with M.

q: Is the 'unstructured search N=8' NMR demo (Table 3) really the largest hardware Grover instance as of 2015, and does the survey's asymptotic story translate into observed hardware speedup at any N with post-2015 superconducting noise budgets?
basis: The paper's experimental table stops at N=8 Grover, which is trivially outperformed by 3 classical function evaluations; the survey does not update this to any 2019-2024 IBMQ / trapped-ion demo, so the practical relevance of the O(sqrt(N)) claim as a function of hardware year is an obvious follow-up.

q: For 'Grover applied to NP-complete Circuit SAT for runtime O(2^{n/2} poly(n))' (Sec. 3), what is the actual constant-factor prefactor of poly(n) when the SAT checker is compiled into an oracle, and is the crossover with modern SAT solvers (CaDiCaL, Kissat) at a value of n that any plausible quantum hardware could reach?
basis: The survey states the O(2^{n/2} poly(n)) headline without quantifying the poly(n) prefactor; our replication used a trivial 1-of-N oracle rather than a real 3-SAT checker, so measuring compiled-oracle depth for an actual 3-SAT instance (n~20) versus modern classical solver runtimes on the same instance would concretely test the survey's implied 'instances of twice the size in comparable time' claim.
